To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have given a sufficient condition for a semigroup of bounded operators on a $W^*$-algebra to induce an analytic or an $R$-semigroup on the corresponding $L^p(\mathcal{W},E)$ spaces.

we provide a sufficient condition on an operator space and on a von Neummann algebra, which ensures that there is a bounded analytic or R-analytic semigroup on the vector valued $L^p$, which is a generalization of the results by M. Junge and Q. Xu.

we have given sufficient conditions on an $E$ and an $M$ to guarantee that the tensor product of the $H^\theta$-calculus of a semigroup on $M$ and an operator space $H^\theta(E)$ is an $H^\theta(\Sigma_\theta(E))$-calculus for the tensor product semigroup on $L^p (M,E)$.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the theory of semigroups of linear operators on noncommutative vector valued $L^p-$spaces.
the study of analytic and $R$-semigroups on vector-valued noncommutative Lp-spaces.
the study of the vector valued non-commutative $L_p$-spaces $L_p(M,E)$, which are the non-commutative analogs of the classical non-commutative vector valued $L_p$ spaces $L_p(\Omega,E)$.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the noncommutative functional calculus is a natural and powerful tool to deal with semigroups of operators in a von Neumann setting.

the $H^\iota(\Sigma_\theta) $ calculus is available for the generators of bounded $C_0$-semigroups on $L^p(A,E)$ whenever $A$ is a von Neumann $W^\ast$-algebra, $1 < p < \infty$ and $E$ is a dual operator space.

, if $M$ is a von Neumann factor and if $E$ is a finite or an ultraproduct of finite operator spaces then $T_t \otimess Id_E$ extends to a $R$ - analytic semigroup on $L^p (M,E)$ for every $p \in (1, \infty )$.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the noncommutative setting, we are able to extend the results of Junge, Le Merdy and Xu to semigroups on the vector valued $L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$-spaces and, moreover, we are able, under some additional assumptions on the semigroup, to extend the results to the vector valued non-commutative $L^{1, \infty}$-spaces.

we extend some of the results in the book by C. Le Mermy and Q. Xu [1] from the case of the noncommutative Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb{B}_n)$ to the case of the vector valued noncomutative $L^{p}$ spaces $L^{p}(M,E)$, for any $1 < p <\infty$.

we give a complete characterization of when an operator semigroup on a von Neuman algebra $M$ generates a bounded analytic semigroup on the noncommutative vector valued $L^p-$spaces $L^p (M,E)$, where $E$ is an arbitrary operator space.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the semigroups $(T_t \circ \varphi)_{t \nonumber\geq 0} \subset \mathcal{B}(M)$ are bounded analytic or $R$- analytic, for a large class of functions $\varphi$ on the unit disc, if and only if the semigroups on the $L^p(\mathcal{M})$-valued noncommutative spaces are bounded analytic or respectively $R$-anaytic

we can use the $R$-boundedness of a semigroup of bounded linear operators $A$ on a von Neuman algebra $M$ together with the noncommutative martingale type $p$-space $(M,\mu)$ to obtain the existence of a bounded analytic or $R$-semigroup $(T_t)_{t \in [0,\infty)}$ on $M$ such that $A$ and $T$ have the same generators.
the noncommutative vector valued $L^p-$space is the natural setting for the theory of analytic semigroups.
